document.title: National Wealth and Human Capital Decentralization Bill Legal Provenance Ledger

claims.text: Article 39(b) and 39(c) of the Constitution direct the State to distribute material resources and prevent wealth concentration to common detriment.

authorities.title: Constitution of India
authorities.issuer: Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India

claims.subsequent_history_checked: Upheld and affirmed in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) and Sanjeev Coke (1983).
claims.limitations: Directive Principles require statutory enactment for enforcement.

claims.text: Parliament has legislative competence over taxes on the capital value of assets under List I Entry 86.
claims.subsequent_history_checked: Wealth Tax Act 1957 was enacted under this entry before repeal in 2015.
claims.limitations: Excludes agricultural land, which falls under State List Entry 46/49.
claims.reviewer_action: Verified against Seventh Schedule of Constitution of India.

claims.text: Citizens enjoy fundamental rights to move freely and reside anywhere in India under Article 19(1)(d) and 19(1)(e).
claims.subsequent_history_checked: Controlled by basic structure doctrine and strict proportionality tests.
claims.limitations: Prohibits coercive internal mobility restrictions or forced human capital relocation.
claims.reviewer_action: Verified against Part III of the Constitution.
